title: How to Exist
excerpt: Here’s an experiment for a true daredevil. Sit there for a three minutes, following two rules:
content_html:
Here’s an experiment for a true daredevil.

Sit there for a three minutes, following two rules:

  1. Don’t do anything.
  2. Be content.

By “don’t do anything,” I mean don’t move, don’t fidget, don’t indulge any thoughts or daydreams. You’re allowed to breathe, and blink.

By “be content,” I mean be completely okay with your experience of doing nothing. Don’t try to change anything, and don’t get impatient with what’s happening. Be completely okay for three minutes.  

Try that now. See how long it takes before you’re dying for it to be over.

It’s oddly difficult to do nothing, and while you’re doing nothing, it’s oddly difficult to feel at ease. There’s such a strong urge to do something: look around the room, rehash a conversation, explore your incisors with your tongue, wiggle your toes, anything. When you stop doing everything and just exist, you almost feel like you’re dying.

This is a crazy thing to notice after having been alive so many years — that your existence itself is so much to bear. There’s always something wrong, even when everything’s fine. It’s as if you can only bear the present moment when you’re trying change it into something else.

This is the strange condition of the human being. It’s allergic to its natural habitat, which is the present moment. In order to cope with this allergy, it perpetually seeks things: feelings and experiences that are not yet present. It wants to always be getting the hell out of here.

You might think that you’re free from this problem sometimes, at least in those moments when you get the thing you’re seeking. Say you’re finally eating the cookie-dough ice cream flurry you looked forward to all day. If you pay close attention as you eat it, you’ll notice that you want to move past this moment too. Lingering on any one spoonful too long becomes unbearable. There’s a powerful drive to go on to the next one. That’s why you ordered a Large.

This most fundamental problem of human life is so easy to overlook because our entire lives are made of the coping strategy. So much of what we seek is solely to flee the experience of being here. People buy things they don’t need, start fights with their partners, eat when they’re not hungry, and scroll miserable and inane content, just to escape the feeling of existence as it already is.

Notice the powerful urge to sip your drink or fiddle with something when the conversation dies at a dinner party. Or how quickly your phone comes out when there’s an unexpected wait. Existence without doing is brutal!

Each year, roughly 100 firefighters are convicted of arson in North America, often on multiple counts. Most often they are young, new firefighters, frustrated by the lack of action.

And hilariously, from a 2014 study on doing nothing:

In 11 studies, we found that participants typically did not enjoy spending 6 to 15 minutes in a room by themselves with nothing to do but think, that they enjoyed doing mundane external activities much more, and that many preferred to administer electric shocks to themselves instead of being left alone with their thoughts.

Even thinking is often a sneaky way of escaping the existence; rumination isn’t so much about trying to solve your problems, as it is about going elsewhere in your mind to escape anxiety and uncertainty. Apparently, electric shocks work even better.

How to become more comfortable with existence

You can develop the ability to exist a lot more comfortably. You do it by practicing existing, a few seconds at a time, without trying to change anything about how existence feels right now.

Basically you sit, do nothing, and notice how it feels to do nothing. (It will probably feel subtly weird and unsettled.) You then see if you can completely embrace these feelings, without the usual squirming and looking elsewhere. But you’ll do it only for a few seconds at a time, using your breath as a measuring stick.

Here’s how to do it without feeling overwhelmed:

(If you have PTSD or any other psychiatric disorder, check with a professional before you do this.)

Sit, eyes open or closed, and relax your body as completely as possible. Take long, easy breaths. Relax every muscle you can. Just do your best.  

When you’re ready, breathe in while keeping the body supple like that. Open to every feeling that occurs during the inbreath: tingling, weirdness, unsettledness, doubt, whatever. Let the whole experience wash over you like warm surf, for that few seconds it takes to inhale.

Let it go. Give yourself a moment.

When you’re ready, do it again: embrace the entire experience of one inbreath. Just let the whole experience happen to you – no need to study it, or figure it out. Just embrace the whole bouquet of feelings, for the few seconds it takes. Push away nothing, just for that few seconds of breathing in.

Once you can do that decently well (no need to be perfect), try the same thing but with an outbreath. Stay relaxed and open throughout the length of one whole outbreath. No defending, no tensing. Be a human puddle.

If you get distracted or frazzled, or you do tense up, that’s okay. Take a few breaths off to recollect yourself. Then try again. You have infinite breaths to try this with.

Repeat this process, one half-breath (an inhale or an exhale) at a time. The half-breath is a small enough span of time that you can usually stay open for the 5-10 seconds it takes. Once you can do it on both an inbreath and an outbreath, see if you can start stringing them together, staying open throughout the whole breathing cycle.

Do this for five minutes at first, including any breaks. Then see what happens when you do it longer, and with fewer gaps. Basically you’ll be resting — just existing and breathing — in that non-defensive state.

Even after one session of this, you might notice you can relax a little more easily, no matter what’s happening.

This is a form of meditation, but I almost want to avoid that word because it makes people get nervous and overcomplicate it. Just think of this practice as existing without fear, for a few seconds at a time. Minimum effective dose is one half-breath.  

Naturally, if you can learn to calm your allergy to existence a bit, life gets easier in nearly every situation. Ordinary experiences like waiting in line, feeling uncertain, being a bit too warm or cold, or not being sure what to do with yourself, become much more tolerable. (And probably most of life contains this sort of minor discomfort.)

Regular practice keeps your allergy symptoms mild. Neglecting it makes them come back.

In particular, you might notice much less of a need to entertain or distract yourself. Escape-driven habits like doomscrolling, random snacking, nail-biting, (arson?), and rumination become less magnetic. When plain old existence feels okay, there’s so much you no longer need to do.

sentences.en: When you’re ready, breathe in while keeping the body supple like that.
sentences.zh: 当你准备好后，吸气，同时保持身体柔软。

sentences.en: Open to every feeling that occurs during the inbreath: tingling, weirdness, unsettledness, doubt, whatever.
sentences.zh: 接受吸气过程中出现的每一种感觉：刺痛、奇怪、不安、怀疑等等。

sentences.en: Let the whole experience wash over you like warm surf, for that few seconds it takes to inhale.
sentences.zh: 让整个体验像温暖的海浪一样冲刷你，在这几秒钟内吸气。

blocks.html_en: Let it go. Give yourself a moment.

sentences.en: Let it go.
sentences.zh: 放手吧。

sentences.en: Give yourself a moment.
sentences.zh: 给自己一点时间。

blocks.html_en: When you’re ready, do it again: embrace the entire experience of one inbreath. Just let the whole experience happen to you – no need to study it, or figure it out. Just embrace the whole bouquet of feelings, for the few seconds it takes. Push away nothing, just for that few seconds of breathing in.

sentences.en: When you’re ready, do it again: embrace the entire experience of one inbreath.
sentences.zh: 当你准备好后，再做一次：拥抱一次吸气的整个体验。

sentences.en: Just let the whole experience happen to you – no need to study it, or figure it out.
sentences.zh: 让整个体验发生在你身上——无需研究或弄清楚。

sentences.en: Just embrace the whole bouquet of feelings, for the few seconds it takes.
sentences.zh: 只需在短短几秒钟内拥抱所有的感觉即可。

sentences.en: Push away nothing, just for that few seconds of breathing in.
sentences.zh: 不要推开任何东西，只是为了那几秒钟的呼吸。

sentences.en: Does not need to practice existing
sentences.zh: 不需要练习现有的

blocks.html_en: Once you can do that decently well (no need to be perfect), try the same thing but with an outbreath. Stay relaxed and open throughout the length of one whole outbreath. No defending, no tensing. Be a human puddle.

sentences.en: Once you can do that decently well (no need to be perfect), try the same thing but with an outbreath.
sentences.zh: 一旦你能做得很好（不需要完美），就尝试同样的事情，但要呼气。

sentences.en: Stay relaxed and open throughout the length of one whole outbreath.
sentences.zh: 在整个呼气过程中保持放松和开放。

sentences.en: No defending, no tensing.
sentences.zh: 没有防守，没有紧张。

sentences.en: Be a human puddle.
sentences.zh: 做一个人类的水坑。

blocks.html_en: If you get distracted or frazzled, or you do tense up, that’s okay. Take a few breaths off to recollect yourself. Then try again. You have infinite breaths to try this with.

sentences.en: If you get distracted or frazzled, or you do tense up, that’s okay.
sentences.zh: 如果您分心或疲惫不堪，或者确实紧张，那也没关系。

sentences.en: Take a few breaths off to recollect yourself.
sentences.zh: 喘口气，让自己回想起自己。

sentences.en: Then try again.
sentences.zh: 然后再试一次。

sentences.en: You have infinite breaths to try this with.
sentences.zh: 你有无限的呼吸来尝试这个。

blocks.html_en: Repeat this process, one half-breath (an inhale or an exhale) at a time. The half-breath is a small enough span of time that you can usually stay open for the 5-10 seconds it takes. Once you can do it on both an inbreath and an outbreath, see if you can start stringing them together, staying open throughout the whole breathing cycle.

sentences.en: Repeat this process, one half-breath (an inhale or an exhale) at a time.
sentences.zh: 重复此过程，一次半呼吸（吸气或呼气）。

sentences.en: The half-breath is a small enough span of time that you can usually stay open for the 5-10 seconds it takes.
sentences.zh: 半呼吸的时间跨度足够小，通常您可以保持开放状态 5-10 秒。

sentences.en: Once you can do it on both an inbreath and an outbreath, see if you can start stringing them together, staying open throughout the whole breathing cycle.
sentences.zh: 一旦你可以在吸气和呼气时都做到这一点，看看你是否可以开始将它们串在一起，在整个呼吸周期中保持开放。

sentences.en: You, with some practice
sentences.zh: 你，经过一些练习

blocks.html_en: Do this for five minutes at first, including any breaks. Then see what happens when you do it longer, and with fewer gaps. Basically you’ll be resting — just existing and breathing — in that non-defensive state.

sentences.en: Do this for five minutes at first, including any breaks.
sentences.zh: 首先做五分钟，包括休息时间。

sentences.en: Then see what happens when you do it longer, and with fewer gaps.
sentences.zh: 然后看看当你做的时间更长、间隔更少时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Basically you’ll be resting — just existing and breathing — in that non-defensive state.
sentences.zh: 基本上你会在那种非防御状态下休息——只是存在和呼吸。

blocks.html_en: Even after one session of this, you might notice you can relax a little more easily, no matter what’s happening.

sentences.en: Even after one session of this, you might notice you can relax a little more easily, no matter what’s happening.
sentences.zh: 即使经过一次这样的训练后，您可能会发现无论发生什么，您都可以轻松地放松一些。

blocks.html_en: This is a form of meditation, but I almost want to avoid that word because it makes people get nervous and overcomplicate it. Just think of this practice as existing without fear, for a few seconds at a time. Minimum effective dose is one half-breath.

sentences.en: This is a form of meditation, but I almost want to avoid that word because it makes people get nervous and overcomplicate it.
sentences.zh: 这是冥想的一种形式，但我几乎想避免使用这个词，因为它让人感到紧张并使之变得过于复杂。

sentences.en: Just think of this practice as existing without fear, for a few seconds at a time.
sentences.zh: 只要想象这种练习是毫无恐惧地存在的，一次持续几秒钟。

sentences.en: Minimum effective dose is one half-breath.
sentences.zh: 最小有效剂量是一次半呼吸。

sentences.en: Grabbing a few minutes to exist between meetings
sentences.zh: 在会议之间抽出几分钟时间

blocks.html_en: Naturally, if you can learn to calm your allergy to existence a bit, life gets easier in nearly every situation. Ordinary experiences like waiting in line, feeling uncertain, being a bit too warm or cold, or not being sure what to do with yourself, become much more tolerable. (And probably most of life contains this sort of minor discomfort.)

sentences.en: Naturally, if you can learn to calm your allergy to existence a bit, life gets easier in nearly every situation.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你能学会稍微平息一下对存在的过敏，那么几乎在任何情况下生活都会变得更轻松。

sentences.en: Ordinary experiences like waiting in line, feeling uncertain, being a bit too warm or cold, or not being sure what to do with yourself, become much more tolerable.
sentences.zh: 诸如排队等候、感觉不确定、有点太热或太冷、或者不确定自己该怎么办等普通经历都会变得更容易忍受。

sentences.en: (And probably most of life contains this sort of minor discomfort.)
sentences.zh: （也许生活的大部分时间都包含着这种轻微的不适。）

blocks.html_en: Regular practice keeps your allergy symptoms mild. Neglecting it makes them come back.

sentences.en: Regular practice keeps your allergy symptoms mild.
sentences.zh: 定期练习可以使您的过敏症状保持轻微。

sentences.en: Neglecting it makes them come back.
sentences.zh: 忽视它会让他们回来。

blocks.html_en: In particular, you might notice much less of a need to entertain or distract yourself. Escape-driven habits like doomscrolling, random snacking, nail-biting, (arson?), and rumination become less magnetic. When plain old existence feels okay, there’s so much you no longer need to do.

sentences.en: In particular, you might notice much less of a need to entertain or distract yourself.
sentences.zh: 特别是，您可能会发现不再需要娱乐或分散自己的注意力。

sentences.en: Escape-driven habits like doomscrolling, random snacking, nail-biting, (arson?), and rumination become less magnetic.
sentences.zh: 诸如末日卷轴、随意吃零食、咬指甲（纵火？）和沉思等逃避驱动的习惯变得不那么有吸引力。

sentences.en: When plain old existence feels okay, there’s so much you no longer need to do.
sentences.zh: 当平淡的旧生活感觉还不错时，你就不再需要做很多事情了。

content_html_zh:
这是一个真正的勇敢者的实验。

坐在那里三分钟，遵循两条规则：

  1. 不要做任何事情。
  2. 满足吧。

我所说的“不要做任何事情”，是指不要动，不要坐立不安，不要沉迷于任何想法或白日梦。 你可以呼吸和眨眼。

我所说的“知足”是指对自己无所事事的经历完全满意。 不要试图改变任何事情，也不要对正在发生的事情失去耐心。 三分钟内完全没问题。

现在就试试吧。 看看你需要多长时间才能结束。

奇怪的是，什么都不做是很难的，而当你什么都不做的时候，也很难感到轻松。 有一种强烈的冲动想做某事：环顾房间，重复对话，用舌头探索你的门牙，摆动你的脚趾，任何事情。 当你停止做所有事情并只是存在时，你几乎感觉自己快要死了。

在活了这么多年之后，注意到这一点是一件疯狂的事情——你的存在本身就是如此令人难以承受。 即使一切都很好，总会有一些问题。 就好像你只能忍受当下的时刻，当你试图把它变成别的东西时。

这就是人类的奇怪状况。 它对其自然栖息地过敏，即当下。 为了应对这种过敏，它不断地寻找事物：尚未存在的感受和体验。 它总是想离开这里。

有时你可能会认为你已经摆脱了这个问题，至少在你得到你想要的东西的时候是这样。 假设您终于可以吃到期待了一整天的饼干面团冰淇淋了。 如果你在吃的时候密切注意，你会发现你也想过去这一刻。 任何一勺的停留时间过长都会让人难以忍受。 有一种强大的动力去继续下一个。 这就是您订购大号的原因。

人类生活中这个最基本的问题很容易被忽视，因为我们的整个生活都是由应对策略组成的。 我们所寻求的很多东西只是为了逃离这里的经历。 人们购买不需要的东西，与伴侣吵架，不饿就吃东西，滚动浏览痛苦而无聊的内容，只是为了逃避已经存在的感觉。

请注意，当晚宴上谈话结束时，你会强烈地想喝点饮料或摆弄一些东西。 或者，当出现意外等待时，您的手机能多快拿出来。 不做事的存在是残酷的！

北美每年约有 100 名消防员因纵火罪被定罪，且罪名往往多种多样。 他们大多是年轻的新消防员，因缺乏行动而感到沮丧。

有趣的是，来自 2014 年一项关于什么都不做的研究：

在 11 项研究中，我们发现参与者通常不喜欢在房间里独处 6 到 15 分钟，除了思考之外无所事事，他们更喜欢做日常的外部活动，而且许多人更喜欢对自己进行电击，而不是独自思考。

甚至连思考也常常是逃避现实的一种偷偷摸摸的方式。沉思与其说是试图解决你的问题，不如说是让你的大脑转向其他地方，以逃避焦虑和不确定性。 显然，电击效果更好。

如何让自己更适应存在

你可以培养更舒适地生存的能力。 你通过练习存在来做到这一点，一次几秒钟，而不是试图改变任何存在现在的感觉。

基本上，你坐着，什么都不做，然后注意什么也不做的感觉。 （可能会感觉有点奇怪和不安。） 然后你会看看自己是否能够完全接受这些感受，而不会像平常那样蠕动并寻找其他地方。 但你一次只能做几秒钟，用你的呼吸作为量尺。

以下是如何做到这一点而不感到不知所措：

（如果您患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）或任何其他精神疾病，请在执行此操作之前咨询专业人士。）

坐下来，睁开或闭上眼睛，尽可能完全放松身体。 进行长而轻松的呼吸。 尽可能放松每一块肌肉。 尽力而为吧。

当你准备好后，吸气，同时保持身体柔软。 接受吸气过程中出现的每一种感觉：刺痛、奇怪、不安、怀疑等等。 让整个体验像温暖的海浪一样冲刷你，在这几秒钟内吸气。

放手吧。 给自己一点时间。

当你准备好后，再做一次：拥抱一次吸气的整个体验。 让整个体验发生在你身上——无需研究或弄清楚。 只需在短短几秒钟内拥抱所有的感觉即可。 不要推开任何东西，只是为了那几秒钟的呼吸。

一旦你能做得很好（不需要完美），就尝试同样的事情，但要呼气。 在整个呼气过程中保持放松和开放。 没有防守，没有紧张。 做一个人类的水坑。

如果您分心或疲惫不堪，或者确实紧张，那也没关系。 喘口气，让自己回想起自己。 然后再试一次。 你有无限的呼吸来尝试这个。

重复此过程，一次半呼吸（吸气或呼气）。 半呼吸的时间跨度足够小，通常您可以保持开放状态 5-10 秒。 一旦你可以在吸气和呼气时都做到这一点，看看你是否可以开始将它们串在一起，在整个呼吸周期中保持开放。

首先做五分钟，包括休息时间。 然后看看当你做的时间更长、间隔更少时会发生什么。 基本上你会在那种非防御状态下休息——只是存在和呼吸。

即使经过一次这样的训练后，您可能会发现无论发生什么，您都可以轻松地放松一些。

这是冥想的一种形式，但我几乎想避免使用这个词，因为它让人感到紧张并使之变得过于复杂。 只要想象这种练习是毫无恐惧地存在的，一次持续几秒钟。 最小有效剂量是一次半呼吸。

当然，如果你能学会稍微平息一下对存在的过敏，那么几乎在任何情况下生活都会变得更轻松。 诸如排队等候、感觉不确定、有点太热或太冷、或者不确定自己该怎么办等普通经历都会变得更容易忍受。 （也许生活的大部分时间都包含着这种轻微的不适。）

定期练习可以使您的过敏症状保持轻微。 忽视它会让他们回来。

特别是，您可能会发现不再需要娱乐或分散自己的注意力。 诸如末日卷轴、随意吃零食、咬指甲（纵火？）和沉思等逃避驱动的习惯变得不那么有吸引力。 当平淡的旧生活感觉还不错时，你就不再需要做很多事情了。
